sentences.text: Macrocollum was a relatively small, bipedal dinosaur that measured approximately 3.5 meters in length, stood 1.5 meters high, and weighed around 101.6 kilograms.
The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — is an almost complete and articulated skeleton.
Its genus name, Macrocollum, refers to the animal's elongated neck.
Macrocollum holds the record for being the oldest known dinosaur with evidence of an air sac system.
It is distinguished from other sauropodomorphs by unique skull features, including a promaxillary fenestra in the antorbital fossa and a smooth curve in the supratemporal fossa margin.
Macrocollum was discovered in 2012 at the Wachholz site in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, and the genus was described by Müller et al. in 2018.
The discovery was officially announced in a press conference on November 21, 2018.
There are two recorded fossil occurrences of the only known species, M. itaquii.
The ilia of one paratype specimen were used as a model to study sedimentary compression effects on early sauropodomorph iliac morphology.
Macrocollum is classified as a member of the order Dinosauria and belongs to the suborder Sauropodomorpha.
It belongs to the clade Unaysauridae, alongside Jaklapallisaurus and Unaysaurus, making the family Unaysauridae its parent group.
Macrocollum is considered one of the oldest known dinosaurs, having lived between approximately 225.42 and 225 million years ago during the Norian age of the Late Triassic.

It lived in southern Brazil, which was connected to northwest Africa during the Late Triassic, when most of Earth's landmass was united in the supercontinent Pangaea, which was beginning to split into Laurasia and Gondwana.
